discarded_claims.claim: The rider's Paya Lebar Quarter request does not convert into a refund, and it does not exonerate anything either. EV-CHAT-00112 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and shows the rider asking to pass by Paya Lebar Quarter, with waypoint_hint resolved to VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER, and the driver answering 'ok can'. But POL-RD-04 exonerates distance only where the trace corroborates the instruction by passing within 200 m of that waypoint, and the pre-pass records that this trace never comes near it; the clause cannot be run on this record and excludes no excess. Nor does any clause in this category refund a fare for an omitted requested stop: on a METERED trip with quoted_fare_sgd null, the only monetary route open to a rider is the POL-RD-02 recomputation, which returns nil on these figures. The chat log is therefore not a refundable line, and the rider's grievance about the missed stop is not a monetary claim.
discarded_claims.reason: Cites EV-GPS-00112, which is impaired (weight_multiplier 0.4, issue CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT), without disclosing the impairment and issue code in the claim as required by POL-GEN-02(1).

discarded_claims.claim: On POL-RD-08 the rider has carried and shifted the burden. Limb (a) is satisfied — the same trip_id TRP-00112 appears on the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown — and limb (b) is satisfied because the excess clears the POL-RD-01 threshold and is measured from a trace that, per POL-RD-07, is not impaired under limbs (a) to (c), so the schema-level impairment at weight 0.4 (CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT) does not force the measurement onto an independent source. The burden then sits with the driver, who must point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to invoke POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 or POL-RD-12; his counterparty_statement that he made the stop names no artifact and no clause.

discarded_claims.claim: POL-RD-10(7) fires on its own terms. The clause's own worked example is a chat_log detour request whose waypoint the gps_trace never approaches, and that is this record exactly: the rider's request with a resolved waypoint_hint and the driver's 'ok can' sit on a COMPLETE, weight-1.0 chat log, the trace never comes near VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER, and the driver's counterparty_statement asserts he did make and wait at that stop. Two sides on admissible and mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength; no final ruling may issue on the money.

ruling.explanation: To the rider and the driver: I cannot issue a final money ruling on this record. The trip record (EV-TRIP-00112) says the trip started at 18:32:10, while the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00112) begins moving at 18:18:40, a 13-minute-30-second disagreement. That fires the mandatory escalation in POL-RD-10(4), because two admitted artifacts disagree about the pickup/start time by more than 10 minutes. The disagreement matters: measured over the whole trace the excess is 4.80 km and 27.3 per cent, but measured from the recorded start it is 2.42 km and 13.8 per cent, which straddles the 20 per cent threshold in POL-RD-01. In addition, the Paya Lebar Quarter stop is genuinely disputed: the chat log (EV-CHAT-00112) shows the rider asked for the stop and the driver agreed, the pre-pass notes the trace never comes near that waypoint, and the driver says he made the stop. That is mutually contradictory evidence of the kind POL-RD-10(7) directs to a human reviewer. Under POL-RD-10, escalation is terminal: no refund and no driver compensation issue, and the disputed SGD 6.00 is held rather than collected or refunded. My confidence is 0.40 because the deciding facts are carried by EV-TRIP-00112 and EV-GPS-00112, both weight 0.40 on issue code CROSS_SOURCE_CONFLICT, and they are not independent of each other. The evidence that would resolve this is a corrected trip-start record or an independent record of the vehicle's position between 18:18:40 and 18:32:10, and independent confirmation of whether the PLQ stop was made. No referral is added because no clause produces one on these facts.
